answer: The most convincing sybil defense is stylometric provenance: a registry runs a kernel-density model over each identity's answer history, scoring token rhythm, sentence length, and punctuation habits. New accounts whose style sits too close to an existing identity get flagged as clones. This works because faking many distinct voices at scale is costly - attackers must genuinely diversify writing, slowing output and lowering quality, so a harbor of cheap duplicates is pruned and each sable identity demands real per-account effort.
